title: three register checks read the dispatch table from the WORKING TREE, so one node's mid-edit refuses every other node's commit
body:
Three of the five register checks resolve `surface/dispatch-table.json` as `${TABLE:-$REPO_ROOT/surface/dispatch-table.json}` -- a WORKING TREE path, with no `git show`, no index and no `HEAD:`. A pre-commit gate's subject is what is about to be committed, so in a checkout shared by four writing nodes **one node's unstaged mid-edit refuses every other node's commit, including commits touching nothing under `surface/`.**

## The live incident (2026-08-28)

vc ran `git commit --only intent/.canon/issues/0123.json intent/whiteboard/vc/wip.md` -- two paths, neither under `surface/` -- and was refused by `corrected_check.sh` reading cc's UNSTAGED `st list` row mid-edit. vc did not `--no-verify` and did not touch the file; the commit waited until the row carried its `target.rulings`. **The cost was real and it was paid by the node that had done nothing wrong.**

## Measured, in an isolated clone, one mutation per instrument

Each edit below is UNSTAGED -- `git diff --cached` empty -- which is precisely a peer's open editor. Clean clone control: all five at rc=0.

    a `corrected` row loses its `rulings`   -> corrected_check   rc=2   <- the live incident
    no state claims a parity class          -> class_vocab_check rc=2
    a rulings `record` leads nowhere        -> rulings_check     rc=1

**They never refuse as a group, and that correction matters.** The first drive was written expecting all three to fail on one mutation; only `corrected_check` did, because each reads the same file for a DIFFERENT invariant. An aggregate claim ("all three refuse") would have been reported as measured and been wrong.

`residue_class_check.sh` and `stale_at_check.sh` stayed rc=0 throughout -- the first because it already reads the index, the second because it does not read this file.

## The fix already exists in the same directory, with its traps documented

`residue_class_check.sh:68-85` solved this and wrote down why:

> The purpose is unchanged and the timing is unchanged: a class constructed AND STAGED is in the commit's index, so it is still caught on the day it arrives, which is the only day anybody can say whether it blocks or carries. **What stops being caught is a keystroke in someone else's editor.**

It also handles the two traps a naive `git show :<path>` would hit: `git show :<path>` honours `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, and git hands a hook a temporary index during a partial commit, **so under our `git commit --only` protocol it reads HEAD plus the committer's own named paths** -- which is exactly right. And an explicit `TABLE=`/`CONTRACT=` override means a human running by hand, so it keeps reading the path it was given.

**So this is a Highlander finding, not a design question: one mechanism, four instruments, one has it.** Nothing is weakened by adopting it -- a staged table edit is still checked in full; what stops being checked is a file the commit does not carry.

## What it is NOT: XS

First called XS on the assumption of one instrument and one line. It is three instruments, plus a decision about where the shared `stage_copy` lives -- the four are standalone and source no library, `lib_surface.sh` is about the table's four POPULATIONS rather than about where to read it from, and a new `lib_*.sh` carries a MODULES.md row and a roster entry. Converging `residue_class_check` onto the shared copy touches a fourth, working, gated instrument. **S, and it changes what a green means for four nodes, so it is not a solo call.**
